profile.summary: PromoterAI is a deep learning model from Illumina that predicts how a variant in a gene promoter changes that gene's expression. It takes a list of variants (chromosome, position, reference and alternative allele, strand) and a reference genome, and adds a score between -1 and 1 to each variant: negative values mean lower expression and positive values mean higher expression. The authors built it to find noncoding promoter variants that may explain rare genetic diseases.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: PromoterAI is a convolutional network written in TensorFlow and Keras. The code first projects one-hot DNA (4 channels) with a 1-wide convolution, then stacks blocks that each apply a dilated depthwise convolution and a two-layer dense step, with batch normalisation and residual connections. The README's training command uses 24 blocks of width 1024, a 20,480-base input and a 4,096-base output. The model is first trained to predict regulatory profiles stored as bigWig tracks around transcription start sites, optionally across several species, and is then fine-tuned on a GTEx variant file. For variant scoring, a twin wrapper runs the model on the reference and the alternative sequence and averages the difference between the two predictions.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The Python package is at version 1.0rc6 in the repository read here. In June 2025 the authors said they had released the code and precomputed scores but not the model weights. In September 2025, answering an issue titled 'Pretrained model weights release', they said the download link is sent by email after the licence agreement linked from the README is completed. The sources read do not name or version the distributed weights, so a result should name the package version, the repository commit, the model folder used and the input length (the README uses 20480).

sections.title: Scores and thresholds
sections.body: Scores run from -1 to 1. The README recommends cut-offs at 0.1, 0.2 and 0.5 in absolute value. Because a promoter variant acts through one gene's strand, each variant row needs a strand; if it is unknown, the README says to score both strands as separate rows and combine the results. Precomputed scores for all human promoter single nucleotide variants are available for academic and non-commercial research after the licence agreement.

strengths.text: Works from plain variant coordinates and a reference genome, and handles both single nucleotide variants and left-normalised indels.

quotes.text: Indels must be left-normalized and without special characters.

strengths.text: Gives a signed score, so a user can tell predicted loss of expression from predicted gain, and the README gives thresholds to apply.

The authors report that variants it flags show outlier RNA and protein expression and strong negative selection, and that they confirmed effects with reporter assays (the authors' claims, from the paper abstract).

quotes.text: produce outlier expression at both the RNA and protein levels in thousands of individuals and that these variants experience strong negative selection in human populations
validated their functional impact through reporter assays

strengths.text: Training, preprocessing and fine-tuning code is included, along with the benchmark and training annotation files, so the model can be retrained.

run_guide.summary: Install PromoterAI and score a small variant file against a reference genome, using a model folder obtained under the licence agreement.
prerequisites: Python 3.8 or later, with TensorFlow 2.13 to 2.15 and Keras 2 (installed by pip).
CPU or GPU; tested on H100 and A100 GPUs.
A trained PromoterAI model folder, sent by email after completing the licence agreement linked from the README. Noncommercial use only under the PolyForm Strict licence.
A reference genome FASTA file matching the variant coordinates.
